analysis: The supplied change is limited to the test file provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/Inference/Engine/EngineV2KVBackendGateTests.swift. Changed ranges are base 713-714 and 720-721, head 713-714, 720-724 and 729-754. The change adjusts the pagedPoolLocksStepWithSchedulerConfig test around line 713. It now expects Gemma 4's wide plain prefill chunk (EngineV2Factory.widePrefillChunkTokens) to replace the default solo-prefill stripe, with soloPrefillStripeTokens == nil and the pool maxPrefillChunk equal to defaultSoloPrefillStripeTokens. It also adds a new test, widePrefillChunkKeepsPagedPoolGeometry, whose body is truncated in the patch excerpt. No production source is changed in the supplied units. I found no change to authorization, attestation, encryption, key handling, the SSD prefix cache (T-041), the coordinator/provider WebSocket, or the other trust boundaries; the tests only assert existing KV-backend selection, fallback and refusal behavior. Test fixtures use temporary directories, ephemeral keys and /dev/null for the guard store; none of this affects production. Remaining questions for integration: the production change behind these test edits is not in this batch. It would alter the scheduler prefill chunk and the paged pool maxPrefillChunk lockstep. That lockstep matters for availability, because a PagedSequenceKV precondition violation kills the process. The paged pool must therefore be sized from max(prefillChunkSize, stripe), and that reasoning should be confirmed in the factory code. The truncated patch also leaves the new test's remaining assertions unseen. I cannot judge these safety properties from the tests alone, so I am setting needs_deeper_review to true.
